To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the chromatin structure of unintegrated HIV-DNA is different from the chromatin structure associated with integrated HIV-DNA, and that this chromatin structure contributes to the silencing of unintegration DNA by preventing RNAP II recruitment.

1) histones are rapidly and efficiently loaded on HIV DNA after its synthesis and import in the nucleus; 2) the chromatin architecture of unintegrated HIV genome is characterized by an increased nucleosome density and a nucleosome present in the DNase hypersensitivity region of the LTR; and 3) the nucleosome covering the LTR DNase hypersensitivity site is responsible for the silencing of unintegrate HIV genome by preventing transcription initiation by RNAPII.
histones are rapidly incorporated on unintegrated HIV DNA and that a nucleosome covering the DNase hypersensitivity site contributes to the transcription repression of unintegrated HIV.

the histone loading on unintegrated HIV DNA is a dynamic process that depends on the viral life cycle.

the presence of Nuc0 and/or Nuc2 on unintegrated HIV DNA is associated with the absence or low levels of active histone marks and RNAPII at the LTR, suggesting that the transcriptional silencer NucDHS is responsible for the transcriptional silening of unintegrated HIV.
the presence of Nuc-DHS is a marker of transcriptional silencing and is lost when RNAPII is recruited to the LTR, as in integrated HIV-1 genomes.
